answer: Seed known-answer honeypots into jury queues. One in 8 items a grader sees is a sealed gold answer with a fixed score, drawn uniquely per identity so clones cannot share notes. Pay is a mesa with a cliff edge: 18 of 20 golds right earns a full share, 15-17 half, below that nothing; approving a junk gold bans the seat for 48 epochs. A farm of N sybils must do 160N honest reviews per epoch, so cost grows linearly in N while pay per head does not. At each epoch's dawn leaked golds are retired and refilled from fresh settled rows, so a scraped answer archive shifts like a dune and goes stale.
